title: Policy Eval Constraint Prioritization & Explainability Log Cheat Sheet
body:
Purpose
This note is an approachable internal cheat sheet for engineers working on the policy evaluation engine: how we prioritize constraints, compute composite scores, structure explainability logs, and how control-plane routing policies interact with multi-region fallbacks. It is intentionally pragmatic — quick heuristics, common pitfalls, and small examples for debugging production traces.

Scope and audience
- Audience: platform eng, runtime, SREs, and solutions eng debugging policy failures or interpreting explainability traces.
- Not meant as a final spec; it documents current behavior, intended invariants, and recommended debugging steps.

High-level model in one paragraph
Policy evaluation takes a request (route metadata, model candidate list, capacities, tenant policy) and runs a sequence: constraint filtering -> soft scoring -> score fusion & normalization -> decisioning (accept/reject/route/degenerate-fallback). Constraints are frequently typed (hard vs soft) and may originate from multiple places (tenant, global safety, regional capacity guardrails). Control-plane routing applies routing policies after evaluation to map a decision to a physical endpoint (hosted, dedicated pool, region).

Constraint taxonomy and ordering (practical heuristics)
- Hard constraints (must be enforced, short-circuit): data residency, encrypted-mode-only flag, banned-model-list, SLA-tier deny rules. If any hard constraint fails, the evaluation returns a denial code plus the dominant constraint id.
- Tiered soft constraints (scored, not fatal): latency-target, cost-budget, quality-confidence, vendor-preference. These are converted into numeric penalties or bonuses and folded into a composite score.
- Origin priority: some constraints have higher provenance priority. By default: tenant-explicit > org-policies > runtime-defaults > region-heuristics. If a tenant explicitly sets allowlist/denylist, that beats global preferences.
- Constraint interaction heuristics: prefer conservative resolution (i.e., higher-privilege constraints override lower ones). Use a last-wins only for non-conflicting boolean toggles; otherwise escalate to explicit conflict-resolution step to produce an explainability item requiring operator review.

Score computation (practical formula)
We use an additive penalty model with normalization to [0,1] where higher is better. Rough steps:
1) Base utility: base_score = model_quality_predicted (0..1) * weight_quality
2) Latency penalty: penalty_latency = sigmoid((p99_latency - target)/scale) * weight_latency_penalty
3) Cost penalty: penalty_cost = min(1, cost_per_token / cost_threshold) * weight_cost_penalty
4) Region bonus/penalty: region_affinity = 1 - region_distance_factor
Final raw score = base_score - (penalty_latency + penalty_cost) + region_affinity
Normalize: final_score = clamp((raw_score - min_possible) / (max_possible - min_possible), 0, 1)
Notes: weights are per-tenant or fall back to org defaults; scale parameters come from profiling telemetry for the model family. The formula above is intentionally simple for interpretability; heavy-handed ML models may be introduced but must emit same explainability fields.

Explainability log schema (compact, line-oriented)
- Each evaluation emits an explainability log: a single newline-delimited JSON object per event in the pipeline (we keep one top-level summary and multiple step records). For readability we use short keys. Minimal required fields in summary: eval_id, request_id, tenant_id, route_id, top_choice, top_score, decision, timestamp, region_hint.
- Each step record includes: step_id, parent_eval_id, type (constraint|score|fusion|decision|controlplane), key, value, numeric_score (if applicable), reason, provenance (tenant|org|runtime|region), latency_ms.
Example summary line (pseudo):
{ "eval_id":"e-9a2", "req":"r-1234", "tenant":"t-77", "route":"chat-gpt-compat", "top_choice":"m-7b-q4", "top_score":"0.73", "decision":"route-hosted-us-west-2", "ts":"2025-01-12T18:32:07Z", "region_hint":"us-west-2" }
Example step lines (pseudo):
{ "step":"s1", "eval":"e-9a2", "type":"constraint", "key":"data_residency", "value":"fail", "numeric":0, "reason":"tenant_policy:eu-only", "prov":"tenant", "lat_ms":2 }
{ "step":"s2", "eval":"e-9a2", "type":"constraint", "key":"p99_latency", "value":"ok", "numeric":1, "reason":"p99_est:40ms <= target:60ms", "prov":"runtime", "lat_ms":5 }
{ "step":"s3", "eval":"e-9a2", "type":"score", "key":"base_quality", "numeric":0.85, "reason":"eval-model:m-7b-q4", "prov":"model-scoring", "lat_ms":12 }
{ "step":"s4", "eval":"e-9a2", "type":"fusion", "key":"final_norm_score", "numeric":0.73, "reason":"weights:tenant-defaults", "prov":"fusion", "lat_ms":1 }

Key explainability invariants to maintain
- Determinism for the same inputs + config: identical explain logs must be produced if the inputs and policy configs are the same. If non-determinism is introduced (sampling, asynchronous capacity checks), mark the explainability log with a non_deterministic flag and include seed/state.
- Minimal but sufficient: logs should be compact but include the minimal provenance and numeric values necessary to reproduce the score offline. Omit raw prompts and PII; logs may include model ids, hashes, and feature summaries only.
- Cost-sensitivity: include estimated cost_per_token and cost_bucket so ops can understand economic tradeoffs in decisioning.

Common debugging patterns and quick checks
- If a request is unexpectedly denied: check for hard constraint failing step (search step.type==constraint and numeric==0). If found, inspect reason/provenance string for tenant vs org.
- If score seems low but constraints OK: examine step.type==score entries for base_quality vs latency penalties. Look at latency_ms per step to detect stale p99 estimates.
- If inconsistent across regions: compare region_affinity and region-distance heuristics. Often misconfiguration of region_distance table is the culprit.
- If explain logs missing fields: confirm that the control-plane feature flag "emit_explainability" is enabled for that deployment and that log sampling is not dropping top-level summaries.

Multi-region control-plane interactions (practical rules)
- Pre-routing vs post-routing checks: we perform constraint evaluation in the logical request context (pre-routing) to get candidate model variants and scores. Control-plane then resolves a physical endpoint using routing policies (region affinity, capacity). Some constraints are re-checked post-routing (e.g., per-pool capacity) and can trigger automatic fallback or backoff decisions.
- Fallback semantics: the control-plane exposes ranked fallback sets per route. If the top physical pool is out-of-capacity, the engine will re-evaluate scoring only if the fallback changes the relevant constraints (e.g., region residency). Otherwise, it uses a cached fusion step with a cost delta applied.
- Cross-region safety: when tenant policy forbids cross-region processing, the control-plane must return a deny before routing. That denial is emitted as a hard-constraint explain step with provenance "tenant".

Rollout considerations for new scoring parameters
- Always ship new weight changes behind a feature flag + percentage rollout. Explain logs must include the active weight-set id so we can correlate score deltas.
- When enabling an ML-based reranker, run in shadow mode for at least 48h and compare top_choice divergence histogram in explain logs (metric: fraction where shadow.top != live.top).

Performance & telemetry guidance
- Explain logs are compact; avoid logging full per-token traces unless a dedicated incident mode is enabled. Typical explain bundle should be <1KB.
- Emit counters: evals_total, evals_denied_hard, evals_denied_soft_thresholded, avg_fusion_latency_ms, explain_sample_rate. These should be exported to our metrics backend.

Checklist for PRs touching policy-eval internals
- Include a deterministic unit test that simulates identical inputs and asserts identical explain steps (or flagged non_deterministic).
- Add migration notes for any change to default weights or region distance table.
- Update the explainability schema docs and add an example explainability trace to the testdata folder.
- Confirm privacy review if you add additional request-derived features to logs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we standardize on a schema version field in the evaluation summary? (Yes, plan to add v field.)
- How to encode composite provenance chains succinctly when multiple policies contribute to a single constraint? (Proposal: provenance: [ordered ids] but that requires nested arrays; alternative: provenance_chain string with delimited ids.)
- Explore a compact binary proto for explain logs for high-throughput internal ingestion.

Appendix: Short example trace (human readable)
Eval e-20250112-01 for req r-8f3
- Step constraint: tenant_data_residency == eu-only => fail -> decision DENY (reason tenant policy).
- Step summary: top_choice=null top_score=0 decision=deny_hard ts=2025-01-12T10:03Z
If this is seen in production: check tenant policy toggle UI, inspect policy history, contact tenant owner before changing runtime defaults.

End of cheat sheet
If something here contradicts other platform docs, mark that section with a comment and tag me (Priya) on the Confluence page; we'll reconcile and update canonical spec.
